import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/moran_global_no2crime_crime_second_half_2014.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

boroughs = df['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}
values = df['value'].values

# Build binary weights matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W[i, j] = 1.0

W_sum = W.sum()
x = values
x_mean = x.mean()
z = x - x_mean
numerator = np.sum(W * np.outer(z, z))
denominator = np.sum(z ** 2)
I_obs = (n / W_sum) * (numerator / denominator)
print('Observed Moran I (binary):', I_obs)

# 5000 permutations
n_perm = 5000
np.random.seed(123)
I_perms = np.empty(n_perm)

for i in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    num_perm = np.sum(W * np.outer(z_perm, z_perm))
    I_perms[i] = (n / W_sum) * (num_perm / denominator)

p_value = np.mean(I_perms >= I_obs)
print('One-tailed p-value (5000 perms):', p_value)

# Also compute row-standardized version
k = W.sum(axis=1)  # degree of each node
W_row = W / k[:, None]
W_row_sum = W_row.sum()
print('Row-standardized W sum:', W_row_sum)
numerator_row = np.sum(W_row * np.outer(z, z))
I_obs_row = (n / W_row_sum) * (numerator_row / denominator)
print('Observed Moran I (row-std):', I_obs_row)

I_perms_row = np.empty(n_perm)
for i in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    num_perm = np.sum(W_row * np.outer(z_perm, z_perm))
    I_perms_row[i] = (n / W_row_sum) * (num_perm / denominator)

p_value_row = np.mean(I_perms_row >= I_obs_row)
print('One-tailed p-value row-std (5000 perms):', p_value_row)
```

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/moran_global_no2crime_crime_second_half_2014.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Drop City of London
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['value']).copy()
dropped_borough = 'City of London'
print('Dropped borough:', dropped_borough)
print('Clean df shape:', df_clean.shape)

# Filter adjacency
adj_clean = adj[(adj['borough'] != dropped_borough) & (adj['neighbor'] != dropped_borough)].copy()
print('Clean adj shape:', adj_clean.shape)

boroughs = df_clean['borough'].tolist()
n = len(boroughs)
print('n:', n)

borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}
values = df_clean['value'].values

# Build binary weights matrix
W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)
for _, row in adj_clean.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W[i, j] = 1.0

# Verify symmetry
diff = (W != W.T).sum()
print('Asymmetric entries:', diff)

W_sum = W.sum()
x_mean = values.mean()
z = values - x_mean
denominator = np.sum(z ** 2)
numerator = np.sum(W * np.outer(z, z))
I_obs = (n / W_sum) * (numerator / denominator)

print('Observed Moran I:', I_obs)
print('Expected I under randomization:', -1.0 / (n - 1))

# 5000 permutations
n_perm = 5000
np.random.seed(42)
I_perms = np.empty(n_perm)

for i in range(n_perm):
    z_perm = np.random.permutation(z)
    num_perm = np.sum(W * np.outer(z_perm, z_perm))
    I_perms[i] = (n / W_sum) * (num_perm / denominator)

p_value = np.mean(I_perms >= I_obs)
print('One-tailed p-value (5000 perms):', p_value)
print('Mean permuted I:', I_perms.mean())
print('Std permuted I:', I_perms.std())
print('95th percentile permuted I:', np.percentile(I_perms, 95))
```

Using a symmetric binary adjacency matrix representing 150 neighboring pairs, the observed Moran’s I is 0.2602. Under complete spatial randomness the expected value is about –0.032. A permutation test with 5,000 random shuffles produced a one-tailed p-value of 0.002, meaning only 0.2% of random spatial arrangements yielded an I at least this high.
